extracted.intended_audience: researchers applying for NIAID (NIH) research career development (K) awards
extracted.subtask_description: Summary of NIAID-specific funding, duration, salary/research support limits, and effort/renewal policies applicants must meet when planning or applying for K (career development) awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fringe benefits included
rubrics_metrics.description: All NIAID K awards include fringe benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum salary caps by K award type
rubrics_metrics.description: Maximum salary $100,000 for K01 (parent), K08, K25, K99/R00, and K23. For K24s, salary is based on full-time institutional salary up to the current NIH Salary Cap multiplied by the percentage of effort plus fringe benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the NIH Salary Cap for the applicable institutional cap when calculating K24 salary; apply the percent effort to the institutional salary to determine K24 salary support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum research support (non-salary) caps
rubrics_metrics.description: Maximum research support of $50,000 is available for K25, K01, K99, K08, K23, and K24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research support refers to funds for research-related costs beyond salary/fringe; check specific K announcement for allowable expense details.

rubrics_metrics.name: K22 direct cost limits and allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: K22s provide $150,000 in the first year and $100,000 in the second year. Up to $50,000 of the award can be devoted to the principal investigator’s salary each year; the remainder can be spent for research and other allowable costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget planning for K22s should allocate no more than $50,000/year to PI salary and the balance to research/allowable costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding duration by award type
rubrics_metrics.description: K01, K08, K23, K24, K25 — 3–5 years (junior applicants generally receive 5 years; more senior-level applicants generally 3 years). K22 — 2 years. K99s — NIAID awards up to 2 years (minimum 1 year required). R00s — NIAID awards up to 3 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan career-development and milestone timelines according to the specific award's typical duration; for K01/K08/K23/K24/K25 consider applicant seniority when estimating likely award length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewability and expectation to transition to independent funding
rubrics_metrics.description: K awards are not renewable. NIAID expects K awardees to move on to independent research support such as an R01.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For competing research applications, NIH policy allows award recipients in the last 2 years of their K support (except for K24) to hold concurrent support from their K award and a competing Research Project grant (e.g., R01, R03). Plan grant timing accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum percent-effort requirements by award type
rubrics_metrics.description: K01, K08, K22, K23, K25, and Parent K99 awards require at least 75% effort (9 person months) devoted to the funded K award. The NIAID Physician-Scientist K99/R00 requires at least 50% effort (6 person months). The K24 requires levels of effort between 25% and 50% (3 to 6 person months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although you can use the remaining (e.g., 3 person months for a 75% award) for clinical and other duties, non-federal funds must pay for that time. Ensure effort commitments on the application match institutional appointment and funding sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percent-effort expectation and appointment status
rubrics_metrics.description: The percent effort spent on all K awards is expected to be full-time effort that’s supported by NIAID through the K award; you are typically expected to have a full-time appointment at the organization applying for the grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may meet the K award effort requirement with your full-time institutional position while simultaneously holding another position part-time; confirm institutional appointment and effort certification with your organization and follow NIH guidance (see 'Percent Effort and Concurrent Salary Support' and the Career Development Grants SOP).
